name: Brand identity system governance
one_line: A governed identity system whose rules, controlled marks and assets, approvals, versions, and permitted-use guidance coordinate many outputs; a logo, style value, or single client project without that system remains ordinary creative work or client engagement.

deterministic: A standards or identity manual with coordinated sections for marks, clear space, incorrect use, colour specifications, typography, imagery or voice, and an applicability statement; the cross-asset rule system is the signal, not the word brand.

A controlled asset register or library that maps multiple approved logo/lockup files, colour or type resources, usage status, version identifiers, and distribution or owner information to one identity system.

An approval or governance record that names the identity system, approving authority, exact revision or asset set, effective or superseded state, and permitted use; an approval token without the governed object is insufficient.
A purpose-coherent identity packet containing a standards manual, source master marks, approved exports, asset register, and change or approval record with recurring system identifiers.
A brand-portal or design-system export whose readable manifest includes identity rules, component or asset references, version metadata, and usage restrictions across more than one output family.
needs_llm: deciding whether a document is an operative identity standard for the holder's organisation, a client-facing proposal, a public reference guide, or a one-off campaign brief; the model must cite the role and governance language or return unknown
deciding whether approval applies to the identity system or merely to one campaign asset; the exact object, revision, approver role, and effective or superseded language must be identified
deciding whether a supplied logo pack is controlled organisational identity material or a downloaded reference/template library when provenance and permitted-use language are absent
deciding whether a heterogeneous archive is one identity-system packet when member filenames differ but the manifest and repeated system identifier establish shared governance
separating a client engagement's identity deliverables from the durable identity system itself when the same manual is attached to a statement of work
never_alone: the words brand, branding, identity, guidelines, style guide, logo, mark, colours, palette, typography, tone, approved, final, master, or v3 alone
one logo, wordmark, icon, colour swatch, font file, SVG, AI, PSD, Figma export, or image of a logo alone
a company, client, product, campaign, agency, studio, or person name alone; names can be depicted subjects, counterparties, issuers, or cited examples
a visual similarity, shared filename stem, parent folder called Brand or Guidelines, or a download session
a signed statement of work, invoice, brief, or delivery manifest alone; those may establish client engagement, finance, contract, or handoff functions without a governed identity system
FINAL, APPROVED, LOCKED, effective date, version number, or file extension alone; version_family is universal evidence and approval requires the governed object and role-bearing record
a public brand-guidelines PDF or a blank template with rules but no evidence that it governs the holder's own system

grouping_reasons: one identity system across its standards, source marks, approved variants, asset register, and governance history
one controlled revision family when a new manual supersedes an earlier manual and the exact rule or asset changes are traceable
one approved-use packet when rules, assets, and permission guidance are distributed together to named teams or vendors
no identity group for an isolated logo, campaign artwork, client brief, public reference guide, or downloaded template without system governance evidence

template.why: Empty by binding contract: creative declares no fields. If the schema later adopts project, stage, artifact_type, or client proposals, those remain the shared creative dimensions; identity-system governance is a situation distinguished by its coordinated rule/asset/approval structure, not by a new field or by logo as a folder level. Not time-first: effective dates and version_family describe change history, while the system identity and artifact function make the group intelligible.

observations: sections specify logo construction, clear space, incorrect use, colour values, typography, imagery and digital/print applicability
revision table names an owner, approver and superseded v4.1
must_not_conclude: that every neighbouring Northwind file is governed by this system
that a cited asset is present locally

observations: rows map lockups and colour variants to asset filenames, status, approved use and owner
header names system revision and distribution date
must_not_conclude: that status cells prove legal trademark ownership

observations: multiple named lockup artboards and linked colour resources
same asset identifier appears in the standards manual and register
must_not_conclude: that this is an identity system without the linked governance records

observations: named brand steward approves v4.2 and retires v4.1
message identifies affected marks and distribution audience
manifest contains standards PDF, source marks, web/print exports, font references, usage notes and a revision manifest
repeated system identifier occurs across members
must_not_conclude: member facts from archive paths alone
that every member is readable or approved

observations: labelled client, objective, audience, deliverables and deadline sections
requests an identity manual and logo concepts but contains no operative standards or asset register
must_not_conclude: that a governed identity system already exists

observations: public-looking manual contains logo, colour and type rules
no holder, owner, approval, distribution or system provenance is established
must_not_conclude: that this governs the user's own organisation

observations: single vector mark with version-shaped filename
no rule manual, register, approval record or permitted-use metadata accompanies it
must_not_conclude: that the depicted mark identifies the file owner's organisation

observations: screen chrome and OCR show a portal approval of a named standards revision
no underlying manual is present in the local corpus
must_not_conclude: that screenshot OCR proves the complete rules or assets
that missing EXIF proves screen origin

falls_through_to.why: A readable identity manual or governance decision with no accepted system group remains a durable standalone record.
An incomplete, unsigned, ambiguous, or detached asset/register packet needs review before system facts are accepted.
A public or downloaded brand guide without holder-specific governance evidence is reference reading.
An isolated logo raster or flat export without identity-system evidence is a one-off image, not a system.
A portal or chat screenshot is residual screenshot material unless its own evidence supports a governed packet.

sensitivity_why: Unreleased identity standards, internal approval decisions, distribution controls, vendor-use restrictions, and proprietary source marks may expose business strategy or licensed assets. The rule follows the governed packet, not the word brand or the file extension.
open_question: NJ-BRAND-1: Should a future creative schema expose a compact identity-system field set (for example system/project, artifact type, stage, and governing owner), or should governance remain a template-level structural signal with only universal version and sensitivity facts? Option A enables identity-specific destination proposals; Option B preserves the current empty schema and keeps identity as a governed situation. NJ-BRAND-2: When an identity manual is commissioned for a client, should one file co-activate creative.client-engagement and this template on disjoint role/governance evidence, or should client engagement remain the sole activation and identity be a group subtype?
